summary: Nine-person year-end panel on 2024 trend following: slow, large-market trend beat fast; August V-shaped shock hurt medium speeds; dispersion driven by speed, universe, purity and de-risking. Also vol selling and structured products pinning indices, crowding, whether illiquid markets trend more, market efficiency, AI use, and 2024 mistakes.

coverage.note: intro, agenda, Katie on 2024 trend themes
CTA style factors by speed/size/correlation, Aug 2024 V shock, reversion, vol selling
carry, replication de-risking, simple models, election liquidity and vol selling
structured products, vol supply, correlation, geopolitics (Trump, China)
crowding debate, QIS concentration, finger pointing
vol compression, beta and esoteric markets
illiquid markets and trend, diversification, small market outliers
market maturity, regime shift, breadth, Asness efficiency
efficiency of markets, joint hypothesis, structural change
stock picking efficiency, non-fundamental flows, AI intro

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: Trend fling is a strategy that does really well when we have Trends and honestly the only big Trend we had this year was equities and a couple esot Commodities
claims.claim: Trend following profits in 2024 were limited because only equities and a couple of commodities produced large trends.
claims.direction: trend following gains concentrated in equities and a few commodities
claims.conditions: works when broad, clear trends exist; weak when few markets trend
claims.testable: yes - compare trend P&L by sector in 2024

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the Market moves particularly in fixed income and currencies have been driven by expectations for monetary policy
claims.claim: Fixed income and currency moves in 2024 were driven by shifting monetary-policy expectations, which gave trend followers choppy rather than persistent trends in those sectors.
claims.direction: rates and FX moves reversed with policy expectations
claims.conditions: when markets trade on repeatedly revised central-bank expectations trends in rates and FX are hard to capture
claims.testable: partly - choppiness can be measured but policy-expectation effect is hard to isolate

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the slower Trend Factor so being slow our slow Trend factor is actually up 12% and a 10v fast factor is down 10 or 11%
claims.claim: In 2024 slow trend signals made money (about +12%) while fast ones lost (about -10 to -11%), so lookback speed was the main differentiator.
claims.indicator: slow trend factor vs fast trend factor (CTA style factors)
claims.direction: long slow trend, avoid fast trend in 2024
claims.conditions: when monetary-policy expectations and elections drove noisy short-term moves while the large equity trend persisted
claims.testable: yes - style factor returns by speed

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: actually worked quite a lot better for Trend this year so our size Factor you know also um suggested larger markets did better
claims.claim: Trend strategies earned more in large, liquid markets such as the S&P than in small ones in 2024.
claims.direction: long large-market trend exposure
claims.conditions: one-year observation; the big equity trend drove it

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: correlation was actually negative so negative correlation Factor
claims.claim: The CTA correlation (co-movement) style factor was negative in 2024, meaning trends in less correlated markets did better.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: you're a bit fast but not too fast you're a bit slow but not too slow that by the time you're short the market recovers and you basically get you know the double down
claims.claim: After the quick V-shaped August 2024 shock, medium-speed trend models were hurt because they went short just as the market recovered, whereas very slow or very fast models fared better.
claims.direction: medium-speed trend underperformed; very slow or very fast did better
claims.conditions: fails when a sharp drop reverses within weeks; slow models do not react and fast models exit quickly

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: reversion Dynamics played out quite well uh and I'm talking about crosssectional reversion Dynamics
claims.claim: Cross-sectional mean reversion made money in 2024 in commodities and equities, including around the August shock, helped by skew effects.
claims.direction: long recent losers vs recent winners cross-sectionally

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: in the early part of the Year volatility selling kept on being a good rewarded
claims.claim: Volatility selling was rewarded in early 2024 and less so in the second half.
claims.direction: short volatility
claims.conditions: earned in early 2024 calm; faded in H2 (see August spike)

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the appetite has been and remains brok carry maybe a bit more um conservative following August
claims.claim: Appetite for carry trades became more conservative after the August 2024 unwind.
claims.direction: reduced carry exposure
claims.conditions: after sharp carry unwind

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: replication is tends to be a bit slower than the overall industry because we don't have stop losses and fall controls
claims.claim: Trend replication using a recent return window de-risks more slowly than managers with stop-losses and vol controls, so it lagged on the August 2024 drop but recovered by month-end because it did not cut exposure at the bottom.
claims.direction: slower de-risking recovered after V-shaped event
claims.conditions: helps in sharp V-shaped reversals; hurts in sustained crashes
claims.testable: yes - compare replicator vs CTA index in Aug 2024

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it just felt to me that simple worked a lot better this year that it was that that the major markets tended to be more stable
claims.claim: Simple trend models did better in 2024 because major markets were comparatively stable.
claims.direction: favor simple models in 2024

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: this to them is an incredibly unusual year in that it's been like taking two steps forward and two and a half steps back on across a ton of different trades
claims.claim: A large managed-futures manager described 2024 as unusually whipsawed: many trades went forward then more than reversed.
claims.conditions: choppy year

claims.speaker: unidentified panelist (volatility specialist)
claims.quote: it was an election year and there was massive liquidity pumped into the system as is often the case during election years that's very V suppressing supportive for markets obviously
claims.claim: Election-year liquidity suppresses volatility and supports markets, which in 2024 emboldened volatility selling.
claims.direction: volatility suppressed, markets supported in election years
claims.conditions: election years; the speaker later says liquidity will be less reliable

claims.speaker: unidentified panelist (volatility specialist)
claims.quote: you pair that with ETF tied to yield uh going from in the last two years from uh 25 billion to about 200 billion
claims.claim: Growth of structured products (about $500bn to $1tn issuance a year) and yield-linked ETFs ($25bn to $200bn) adds persistent index volatility supply that pins the index and keeps volatility low.
claims.direction: index volatility suppressed; vol selling structural
claims.conditions: persists while issuance grows; speaker views it as a secular trend
claims.testable: partly - issuance data exist but causal link is hard to test

claims.speaker: unidentified panelist (volatility specialist)
claims.quote: even in August where we had a massive Ball blow up uh it reverted so quickly uh that Ball blow up really came from overseas primarily the ball was incredibly well supplied
claims.claim: The August 2024 volatility spike reversed quickly because US index volatility was well supplied by sellers; the spike originated overseas.
claims.direction: volatility spikes revert fast
claims.conditions: when index vol is heavily sold
claims.testable: partly - can test spike half-life vs vol supply proxies

claims.speaker: unidentified panelist (volatility specialist)
claims.quote: if the index is well supplied and pinned in idiosyncratic where still exists things have to start moving away from each other by definition so that that's what's really been driving the low correlation
claims.claim: When the index is pinned by volatility supply, single stocks must move apart, which creates low correlation (high dispersion) among stocks.
claims.direction: low implied and realized correlation
claims.conditions: when index vol supply is high
claims.testable: yes - index vs single-stock correlation and vol selling proxies

claims.speaker: unidentified panelist (volatility specialist)
claims.quote: in terms of liquidity which is the other factor I find that uh will be much less reliable given uh some of the other macro factors
claims.claim: The liquidity support seen in 2024 is expected to be less reliable in 2025.

claims.speaker: Jim Kasang
claims.quote: if the number one and number two economies uh can get over that divide that will change a lot of things globally
claims.claim: Whether Trump's China stance turns less hawkish (and US-Russia stance softens) is the key geopolitical question, because US-China alignment would change global conditions.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunn
claims.quote: you know yields had been rising have have steadied since that appointment so I think that the Hope in in the markets that he he'll be a steadying uh perspective
claims.claim: Treasury yields steadied after Bessent's appointment because markets hoped for deficit reduction and a stable dollar, with Lutnick and Trump favoring a weaker dollar creating a tension on tariffs, FX and deficit.
claims.indicator: US Treasury yields; Treasury Secretary appointment
claims.direction: yields steadier
claims.conditions: depends on which personality (Trump, Bessent, Lutnick) dominates

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: one of the best performing strategies year to date and that's outside of trend is single stock momentum
claims.claim: Single-stock momentum (long winners, short losers) was one of the best strategies in 2024 outside trend, returning about 44% versus a 10-year range of -7% to +17%.
claims.direction: long past winners, short past losers
claims.conditions: one implementation cited; driven by mega-cap tech and AI winners

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: calling the shots is extremely impossible right and we know the story and I'm not going to go around you know why is it hard for crowding to be predicted when it's going to blow up
claims.claim: Timing the unwind of crowded positioning is essentially impossible, even though concerns about concentration and leverage run all year.
claims.testable: partly - crowding signals are testable but timing has proved unreliable

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: there has been a lot of coordinated positioning but the coordinated positioning has worked and has continued to work
claims.claim: Cutting positions on a crowding measure in 2024 would have lost money because crowded trades kept working.
claims.direction: do not cut on crowding alone
claims.conditions: crowded trades keep performing until a catalyst; one-year evidence

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: the co- movement factor that we look at for Trend was not really a big you know a big factor this year it was really a speed factor that was the biggest differentiator
claims.claim: Trend-following dispersion in 2024 was explained mainly by speed rather than by co-movement.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: there was one article in Bloomberg that was discussed quite um quite substantially talking about oh there's much utilization of those strategies
claims.claim: Claims that quantitative investment strategies (bank QIS) are dangerously concentrated are not visible in the data.
claims.testable: partly - data on QIS growth limited

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it's ctas oh it's Vol scaling oh isk parity there was another FD article that followed after that
claims.claim: After sharp moves such as August 2024, commentators blame CTAs, vol-scaling and risk parity, but this finger-pointing is often not backed by evidence; growth of call-overwriting active ETFs is another flow.
claims.testable: no - blame attribution is hard to test

claims.speaker: unidentified panelist (volatility specialist)
claims.quote: the more of all compression you have I think 2017 that was the lowest realized and implied volatility in history in 120 years history by 30% uh because of the amount of B selling
claims.claim: Longer and deeper volatility compression, caused by heavy vol selling, leads to bigger volatility expansions later, as in 2017 and the summer 2024 build-up.
claims.direction: bigger vol expansion after compression
claims.conditions: when vol selling is heavy
claims.testable: yes - vol of vol vs prior compression

claims.speaker: unidentified panelist (volatility specialist)
claims.quote: positioning particularly of dealers that that we watch uh is very correlated to Trend so the more the more uh you have a trend and things work the more people Pile in and the more concentration happens
claims.claim: Dealer positioning is correlated with trend; as trends persist more participants pile in, building concentration and potential energy for a larger blowup.
claims.conditions: when trends are long-running

claims.speaker: unidentified panelist (volatility specialist)
claims.quote: we are in a period of significant Vault compression happening currently uh really started post election it will probably go through January I would be hesitant in uh you know after January 20th
claims.claim: Volatility compression since the Nov 2024 election likely lasts through January, with risk of a larger vol move after the Jan 20 inauguration.
claims.direction: low vol to January, caution afterwards

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: if you can get something like that in a reasonably efficient way then and and you have the fee budget like why not allocate your dollars to people who are doing really really really esoteric things
claims.claim: Once trend beta is available cheaply via replication or ETFs, investors can spend fee budget on managers trading esoteric, less liquid markets for alpha.
claims.testable: partly - depends on how beta is defined

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: where you were in essence coming as a liquidity provider but often it wasn't about Trend following it was about mean reversion and and and and information asymmetries and you know non-economic players
claims.claim: In semi-liquid markets such as power, returns often came from mean reversion and information asymmetries by acting as liquidity provider against non-economic players, not from trend following.
claims.direction: mean reversion in semi-liquid markets
claims.conditions: needs trading cost capacity

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if you just think about me reversion as kind of like Market making at a slower time frame then you got anything with kind of bigger spreads is going to be kind of wondering around
claims.claim: Mean reversion is slow market making, so less liquid markets with wider spreads should favour it.
claims.direction: mean reversion in illiquid markets
claims.conditions: bid-ask spread large
claims.testable: yes - compare reversion returns by liquidity net of costs

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I've never really actually seen any evidence that um less liquid markets do Trend more
claims.claim: There is no statistically significant evidence that less liquid futures trend more; apparent evidence comes from shorter histories that coincide with strong trend periods.
claims.conditions: comparison of short history to a 50-year history is biased

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the benefit of alss is purely that that you get more diversification simple as that
claims.claim: The benefit of adding alternative markets is diversification, not stronger trends.
claims.direction: add alternative markets for diversification

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: in crypto it's the reverse like less liquid coins seem to to Trend worse
claims.claim: In crypto, less liquid coins appear to trend worse, contrary to the idea that illiquidity helps trend.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: cocoa coffee Ojo Bitcoin um some of the Yen pairs like the pound Yen so I think that um there are certain Trend followers who are focusing in in some of the sort of smaller markets
claims.claim: Smaller trend followers did well in 2024 through idiosyncratic outlier trends in cocoa, coffee, orange juice, bitcoin and yen crosses.
claims.direction: long cocoa, coffee, OJ, bitcoin
claims.conditions: 2024-specific outliers

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: the dominant markets um I think tend to be much more correlated um than some of the alternative assets
claims.claim: Dominant markets are more correlated with each other than alternative assets, so alternative markets bring diversification during a financial decoupling.

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: infant markets tend to be um uh show this prevalence towards trending um conditions and as um as they mature and more and more participants come in of different flavors
claims.claim: Young markets trend more, and as they mature with more participants they become noisier and more mean-reverting, an argument attributed to Perry Kaufman.
claims.conditions: market age effect
claims.testable: yes - trend strength vs market age

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: I put this down to generally a significant regime shift that occurred from about two 20120 onwards um this this change from the the quantitative tightening to the quantitative easing
claims.claim: A 2020 regime shift in monetary policy (QE/QT) boosted idiosyncratic outlier trends and benefited classic trend followers in 2024.

claims.speaker: Neils Kostner Larsen
claims.quote: the ones who trade three or four 500 markets actually their performance is not making any real benefit of that
claims.claim: Managers trading hundreds of markets gain little from outlier moves in a few small markets because each market has too little weight; those who did well traded few markets.
claims.conditions: outlier-driven years

claims.speaker: Alan Dunn
claims.quote: markets had become less efficient over time and um I guess it it it very much is an equity perspective the evidence he presented was looking at valuation factors for different stocks
claims.claim: Cliff Asness argues equity markets have become less efficient because high-valued stocks trade at a premium over cheap stocks for longer than historically expected, as in 2000 and again recently.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunn
claims.quote: the implication for Quant strategies is that that you may go through longer periods of of draw downs but ultimately there should be good opportunities because of these mispricings
claims.claim: Less efficient markets mean longer drawdowns for quant value strategies but eventually larger mispricing opportunities (Asness's drivers: indexing, low rates, social media).
claims.direction: long cheap, short expensive over long horizons
claims.conditions: needs long patience

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: for a lot of asset classes the reason why Trend following is effective is because we don't have good valuations
claims.claim: Market efficiency is a joint hypothesis; outside equities there is no good valuation, which is why trend following works, using price as the valuation measure.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: how different the equity markets are today than they were 30 years ago you know back then in the early 1990s you couldn't get smart people to go into manufacturing
claims.claim: Long-term studies of value versus growth miss structural change: today's leading firms allocate capital better than stock pickers, so old valuation relationships may not hold.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: when I look at for instance like the average activist Target today they're generally pretty great companies maybe with a not terrifically wonderful structure
claims.claim: Stock selection has become more efficient because easy targets (badly run companies, long-term bad and cheap) are rarer; activist targets are now good companies.

claims.speaker: unidentified panelist
claims.quote: the inputs to supply and demand are those flows are increasingly uncorrelated uh unrelated to fundamentals
claims.claim: Prices increasingly deviate from fundamentals because flows (central bank and Treasury liquidity, options, structured products, passive investing, retail meme trading) are unrelated to fundamentals.
claims.testable: partly - flow data hard to isolate

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: you find out that the existing benchmarks which are oftentimes very simple models are fairly effective it's hard it's hard to beat you know what what you may have been using for a long period of time
claims.claim: Machine learning models are only marginally better or worse than simple trend benchmarks, which are hard to beat.

claims.speaker: Jim Kasang
claims.quote: it is a way to uh replace kind of the the low-end work uh not a way to solve big quantitative problems at the end of the day but but that can make you more efficient and lower your costs
claims.claim: AI is useful for aggregating data and basic coding as a cost saver, not for solving core quantitative problems.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the AI models were exactly as bad as the doctors um in terms of interpreting the data
claims.claim: In a medical test on proprietary radiology data, AI models were as bad as doctors, an analogy used to doubt AI will improve investing.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it seems to act in an unbelievably stupid ways a lot of the time and and really is just going to be picking up and amplifying on the biases that we know exist
claims.claim: Given poor, gamed investment data, AI will pick up and amplify biases, so it will not replace models.
claims.conditions: poor data

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: human beings are terrible Market timers and it turns out that these models are pretty good at it
claims.claim: Trend following models beat humans at timing because humans are poor market timers.
claims.direction: systematic over discretionary timing
claims.testable: yes - systematic vs human timing evidence

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: conflating macro you know Trends with market trends
claims.claim: The September 2024 Fed cut was followed by higher long yields, a mistake in assuming Fed cuts shift the whole curve down; macro trends and market trends differ.
claims.indicator: Fed funds rate vs long-term yields
claims.direction: long yields rose after Fed began cutting
claims.conditions: when cuts occur with higher term premium or growth/inflation expectations
claims.testable: yes - yield curve response to cuts

claims.speaker: unidentified panelist
claims.quote: the biggest mistakes is people trying to anticipate uh fed policy and sort of having sort of swinging back and forth between expectations has been the biggest challenge this year
claims.claim: Anticipating Fed policy and swinging between expectations was the main source of mistakes in 2024, including predicting a steeper yield curve.

claims.speaker: unidentified panelist
claims.quote: prices are Primal you know if you know it's just that you're not making any forecast all you're doing is following what prices tell you
claims.claim: Trend following avoids forecast mistakes by following prices, so it is not 'wrong' in the forecasting sense.

claims.speaker: unidentified panelist
claims.quote: I increased my location to Trend following it what turned out to be pretty close to a local maximum
claims.claim: Allocators who raised trend allocation after strong performance bought near a local maximum.
claims.conditions: performance chasing

claims.speaker: Rich Brennan
claims.quote: year to date uh between you know maybe 70% for the year down to you know minus 5% for the year but massive dispersion this year
claims.claim: Trend-following managers' 2024 returns ranged from about +70% to -5% and SG Trend Index is dominated by the largest managers and not representative of the broad community.
claims.indicator: SG Trend index; manager return dispersion

claims.speaker: Katy Kaminski
claims.quote: return dispersion is sort of always underestimated by clients in our space because we all have very high correlation but the range of outcomes are very large
claims.claim: Clients underestimate trend manager dispersion because time-horizon and parameter choices create idiosyncratic return paths despite high correlation.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: manages differ for 3 plus one reasons and I had a conversation with with other about month go on this one number one is speed Katie mentioned it I mentioned it earlier number two is Universe
claims.claim: Trend managers differ because of speed, market universe, purity of trend versus reversion or carry, and discretionary de-risking.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I cannot give zero probability on a systematic manager basically calling the shorts over the weekend I'm actually the risking
claims.claim: Some systematic managers discretionarily de-risked over the weekend of the August 2024 shock, adding to dispersion.
claims.conditions: event risk (NFP, Bank of Japan)

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: small changes in in in parameters would not only result in big near-term dispersion depending on which markets we're over waiting under waiting how we're sizing positions but those often would could extend out over time
claims.claim: Small trend parameter or sector-weight differences produce large dispersion that can persist for long periods, one reason for choosing a simple top-down replication approach.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: I call it uh STM style timing in markets so once you put people into you know a timing bucket you know a market bucket
claims.claim: Classifying managers by style, timing and markets (STM) removes much apparent dispersion in trend following.

claims.speaker: unidentified panelist
claims.quote: I wonder if larger managers this year just simply couldn't get enough exposure to the markets that moved like coffee and cocoa
claims.claim: Large funds hit contract limits and cannot take meaningful positions in small markets, which reduces their benefit from outlier trends and adds to size-based dispersion.
claims.conditions: large AUM
